summary: FX Inline has a real inline-conversion product and a credible parser package, but it still has no revenue surface, no analytics, no billing, no lead capture, and essentially no public traction. The best path to first revenue is a fixed-fee B2B pilot for client-side local-currency price localization, sold using the existing extension as proof.
key_context_inputs_used: docs/revenue-reviews/context/ was missing entirely, so there was no user-provided business ground truth for installs, traffic, revenue, or constraints.
docs/SAAS_ROADMAP.md explicitly keeps billing and backend-managed rates out of scope.
package.json reports version 0.4.1 while public marketplace snippets still show 0.3.6 or even 0.0.0.

recommended_focus.title: Sell one fixed-fee B2B pilot for client-side local-currency price localization
recommended_focus.why: The repo already contains the hard technical asset: on-page price detection and conversion that works on messy DOM. One paying pilot can generate revenue faster than waiting for browser-install scale or building a premium paywall.
recommended_focus.smallest_viable_test: Rewrite the website around one pilot offer, create personalized demos using the existing extension on real prospect pages, and sell one fixed-fee implementation without building subscriptions first.

ranked_monetization_opportunities.title: Fixed-fee pilot for client-side local-currency price localization
ranked_monetization_opportunities.rationale: The current extension can already demonstrate the outcome on real pages. A single buyer closes faster than a consumer paywall from zero installs.
ranked_monetization_opportunities.smallest_test: Use the existing extension to create personalized before/after demos for SaaS pricing pages, travel pages, or price-heavy content pages.

ranked_monetization_opportunities.title: Parser and runtime packaging plus services or licensing
ranked_monetization_opportunities.rationale: The standalone parser package and benchmark scripts are credible technical assets, but packaging is blocked by private package settings and missing licensing.
ranked_monetization_opportunities.smallest_test: After one pilot conversation, extract a smallest embeddable runtime and attach a services offer.

ranked_monetization_opportunities.title: Affiliate content around international shopping, travel, and transfers
ranked_monetization_opportunities.rationale: Wise and Travelpayouts validate referral economics, but FX Inline has no audience, analytics, or content engine yet.
ranked_monetization_opportunities.smallest_test: Launch one use-case landing page and one referral CTA after measurement exists.

ranked_monetization_opportunities.title: Paid consumer extension tier
ranked_monetization_opportunities.rationale: Competing extensions with more scale still struggle on reviews. FX Inline has no traction cushion for a premium launch.
ranked_monetization_opportunities.smallest_test: Only test after trust, installs, ratings, and onboarding improve.

assumptions: The missing docs/revenue-reviews/context directory means there is still no business ground truth for installs, traffic, or monetization constraints.
The user is willing to pursue service revenue or fixed-fee pilots if that is the fastest path to first revenue.
The public marketplace snippets captured this run are directionally accurate even if some store metadata is cached or locale-specific.
There is no hidden analytics or CRM stack outside the repo.
risks: The wrong B2B wedge could waste outreach cycles if the offer is too broad or too weak.
Version inconsistency and missing trust pages can kill response rates before product quality matters.
Performance or false-positive issues on live pilot pages would hurt delivery and credibility.
Launching a premium consumer tier before traction would likely fail and could produce bad reviews faster.

sources.title: FX Inline Chrome Web Store mirror

changed_this_run: click_currency: current Chrome listing showed 384 users, 22 ratings, and 2.0 rating while the official site still pushes one-time lifetime premium.
xe_currency_data_api: verified current public pricing from 799 USD/year to 4499 USD/year depending on plan.
fx_inline_public_metadata: Firefox and Chrome surfaces still lag the repo version.

positive_themes: Users like staying on-page instead of opening a separate converter.
Privacy and no-account positioning helps when the experience works.
Auto mode plus click mode flexibility is appreciated.
negative_themes: Wrong conversions or nonsense values kill trust immediately.
CPU or memory overload on dynamic sites creates harsh feedback.
Manual currency defaults and repeated setup feel slower than opening a website.
Highlight styles and number formatting can hurt readability.
feature_requests: Better decimal and locale formatting controls
trust_concerns: Exposed API keys were explicitly called out in competitor reviews.
Extension privacy claims need visible public support pages.
Version inconsistency makes FX Inline look unfinished.
revenue_relevant_insights: Simplicity, accuracy, and performance drive reviews more than feature breadth.
Bad ratings can coexist with monetization attempts, which makes weak consumer premium dangerous.
Merchant and publisher buyers already pay for localization outcomes elsewhere, so page-layer localization can be sold if positioned correctly.

Serial bottlenecks still remain: choosing the offer, buyer trust, outreach response, and closing a pilot.
Manual payment collection is faster than building subscription infrastructure.
